> Out of curiosity, have you tested compression speed on mobile? I suspect it will be very slow and may not be feasible for a project to actually use this on mobile.

It's fast enough!

Those times are "slow" if you're thinking about rendering and frame times.

However, MoAT has a small thread pool that's responsible for downloading and processing the images, and these times are nothing compared to how long it takes to download the images over the internet.

Encoding as ETC2 the VRAM usage for textures (as reported by Godot's "Texture Mem" monitor) drops by about 60% (going from ~800mb to ~300mb), when doing the 3 room test I've been doing over and over again. :-) So, it seems worth it to me

> You probably want to ask if the stakeholders in export template size are ok with this, you mentioned this was not in the default template so it's probably fine?

Yep, this won't change the official builds; developers need to make a custom build to use this.

> The @BlueCube3310 's work with betsy would work with bptc, but I don't remember the exact files betsy supports for use at runtime compression on the quest 3. If I remember correctly it was some sort of (vulkan) compute shader.
> [...]
> You may need another pr for betsy.

A scons flag for enabling Betsy compression in export templates was already added in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111015

> tl;dr etcpak has poor graphics quality, for aesthetic reasons I would avoid the use of etcpak as much possible.

In this case, I think it's fine. All the non-dynamic textures in the game (ie the ones that aren't downloaded from the Wikipedia) are using ETC2, so this PR allows the dynamic textures to match. And I suspect that compressing ETC2 is faster than Betsy - speed is somewhat important here since this is being done at runtime

I suspect Betsy to be faster than etc2 on the Quest 3 because Betsy is using gpu compute shaders written in a data friendly way versus cpu code in etcpak, but I don't know unless we do an on-device benchmark.

If you're satisfied, feel free to ignore me.

> I suspect Betsy to be faster than etc2 on the Quest 3 because Betsy is using gpu compute shaders written in a data friendly way versus cpu code in etcpak, but I don't know unless we do an on-device benchmark.

In the case of MoAT, we can't do this with GPU compute shaders for two reasons:

- It's using the OpenGL renderer (so no compute)
- We don't have any headroom on the GPU (it's maxed out), we only have cycles to spare on the CPU
